newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour to press on with electoral reform vote.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour to press on with electoral reform vote.

text.p: Britain's opposition leader reaffirmed on Monday he planned to hold a referendum on voting reform if he comes to power at the forthcoming general election, which must be held by May 22.
Monday's Times and Telegraph newspapers said Labour leader Tony Blair was expected to drop the referendum plan.

But Blair told a news conference: "We have made it clear all the way through that we are committed to a referendum and we are committed to it as part of the legislative programme for a first parliament."
Labour is holding talks with the minority Liberal Democrats, whose support it may need after the election to govern, on how to reshape Britain's political institutions.

The minority party suffers badly from Britain's "first past the post" electoral system. At the last election in 1992 it won just 20 seats in the 651-member House of Commons despite polling more than 17 percent of the votes.
The Liberals want a system of proportional representation and have made it clear no deal on future cooperation with Labour can be struck unless there is an agreement on a referendum on voting reform.
Blair has said he has yet to be convinced that proportional representation would be beneficial to Britain.

Labour and the Liberal Democrats have also been discussing plans for assemblies for Scotland and Wales, reform of the British parliament's non-elected upper House of Lords and whether to introduce a freedom of information act.
